lastCompletedStory.title: Review round 2 fix 002: address reviewer finding

openQuestions: US-R2-003 is BLOCKED again on a THIRD consecutive implementer dispatch; nothing in the repo changed across all three dispatches (verified this session: git log -1 --format=%H -- scripts/cam/prd.json is still 3b34b639, predating both prior blocked-dispatch commits, and scripts/cam/prd.json still has the same 8 occurrences of the literal string 'oracle: named-command' at lines 61, 62, 78, 81, 100, 102 -- the same 6 acceptanceCriteria strings named below -- plus the 2 narrative occurrences inside the story's own notes/text fields). The finding (scripts/cam/prd.json:32) is that 6 of this PRD's 25 oracle directives embed a literal 'named-command ' prefix that classifyOracleText (src/supervisor/behavioral-gate.ts:108-125) does not strip, so runBehavioralGate ships `named-command bash -c '...'`/`named-command bun test ...` to the shell and gets exit 127 every time; the reviewer's independent Layer B run confirmed 10 PASS / 6 FAIL(127). The mechanical fix is dropping the literal 'named-command ' prefix from those 6 acceptanceCriteria strings in scripts/cam/prd.json, which no implementer session can make: CAM_WORKER=1 and CAM_SESSION are both set (re-verified via `env` this session), and .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh denies Write/Edit/MultiEdit against any path matching *scripts/cam/prd.json whenever CAM_WORKER=1, unconditionally of what the edit changes (re-read the hook source this session at lines 76-107 to confirm the deny is unconditional, not content-sensitive, and covers only the Write/Edit/MultiEdit tool names -- a raw Bash write is mechanically possible but is documented at scripts/cam/patterns.md:942 and reaffirmed at patterns.md:1064-1066 as NOT an available escape hatch, since it would let a worker self-grade its own acceptance criteria unreviewed). This is the identical CAM-433/CAM-434 dead-end class (scripts/cam/patterns.md:1064-1066), whose explicit rule is: do not keep re-dispatching implementer retries once the dead end is documented once; escalate to an orchestrator/operator (non-CAM_WORKER) session instead. Per the CAM-214 circuit-breaker pattern referenced by the prior dispatch's handoff, this is now N=3 consecutive identical BLOCKED_* outcomes on an unchanged PRD -- the harness's own documented signal to halt auto-dispatch on this story entirely rather than issuing a 4th retry. Exact edits needed, all in scripts/cam/prd.json under userStories[]: US-001 acceptanceCriteria[2] (AC3, line 61) and [3] (AC4, line 62); US-002 acceptanceCriteria[1] (AC2, line 78) and [4] (AC5, line 81); US-003 acceptanceCriteria[4] (AC5, line 100) and [6] (AC7, line 102) -- in each of these 6 strings, replace the substring `[oracle: named-command ` with `[oracle: ` (the trailing `]` and the command text inside are unchanged; only the 'named-command ' token is dropped, e.g. AC3 becomes `... [oracle: bash -c '! grep -q "config.toml with permission_mode" index.ts && grep -q "retry.toml" index.ts']`). Re-running each of the 6 directives without the prefix exits 0 per the reviewer's SECTION 2 hand-verification cited in the story notes.

US-R2-003's own notes flag a second, distinct product/doc mismatch that is explicitly out of scope for this PR (the story notes say it 'belongs in a separate issue'): templates/commands/cam-issue.md:132 and the implementer/reviewer agent contracts display the '[oracle: named-command ...]' prefixed form as the documented spec, while templates/agents/subagent-planner.md:158 and the parser (classifyOracleText) expect the bare command -- so a planner following the documented form will keep emitting unrunnable directives. Not touched by this story; needs its own filed issue.

RECOMMENDATION for the orchestrator/operator: apply the 6-line prd.json amendment described above directly (outside a CAM_WORKER=1 session, matching the precedent commit that resolved the analogous CAM-434 US-R1-003 finding), then re-run cam next so a fresh implementer dispatch of US-R2-003 sees an actually-fixable diff. Do not dispatch a 4th implementer retry against the unmodified PRD.
